title: Field order of GUID byte arrays and canonical UUID text
summary: The first 4, 2, and 2-byte fields of a traditional Windows COM GUID can be stored in little-endian order, and the last 8 bytes are retained in order.
applies: Binary encoding; file and value dumps
detail: The first eight bytes of bytes_le of text 00112233-4455-6677-8899-aabbccddeeff are 33 22 11 00 55 44 77 66.
boundary: The network byte order of RFC UUID is another convention; reversing the entire string will not get the above GUID layout.
relevance: Corresponds the identifier in the binary metadata to the UUID string in the log.
